articles.title: HOW WOULD YOU CONTAIN A PRIVILEGED BUILD ON A SHARED CI RUNNER?
articles.summary:
Container builds and fork pull requests run with elevated privileges on nodes shared with every other job. AWS Nitro Sandboxes contains them instead.

🔒Isolate every job: each runner pod or ECS task runs in its own lightweight VM, managed by the Nitro Hypervisor, so a privileged build never reaches the host

⚡Keep your pipeline intact: a runtime class on EKS [5] or an isolation mode on ECS [6] turns it on, with no image or Helm chart changes

📦 Share instances you already run: pack isolated jobs onto your EC2 instance at no additional charge

TRY THE GITHUB ACTIONS BLUEPRINT - [7]>

articles.title: GOOGLE DONATES AGENT SUBSTRATE AND GVISOR TO THE CNCF TO SECURE AI AGENTS AT SCALE
articles.summary: Google is donating Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF to help run AI agents securely at scale. Agent Substrate separates agent state from compute in pre-warmed Kubernetes pools, which Google says lets agents resume in under 500 milliseconds.

articles.title: INTRODUCING IN-PLACE MIGRATION TO GKE DATAPLANE V2
articles.summary: Google Cloud released in-place migration to GKE Dataplane V2 in preview for VPC native clusters on GKE 1.35 or later. Teams can move from Dataplane V1 without building a parallel cluster, and they can roll back before finalization.

articles.title: KARPENTER V1.15: GPU-AWARE PROVISIONING, SMARTER NODE REPAIR, AND MORE
articles.summary: Karpenter v1.15 adds Dynamic Resource Allocation support to factor GPU topology and networking into provisioning decisions. It classifies node repair as a voluntary disruption that respects Pod Disruption Budgets. The update also introduces a pod deletion cost controller and CEL support for dynamic kubelet configurations.

articles.title: SHIPPING 100+ PRS TO PRODUCTION IN A WEEK
articles.summary: An engineering lead shipped 170 pull requests in a single week by optimizing development loops with AI tooling. Key steps included modernizing CI/CD, moving issue management from Jira to Linear, and building a cloud harness to run orchestrated agents. These changes addressed bottlenecks like slow approvals and inaccurate documentation in the knowledge base.

articles.title: BUILDING PLANETSCALE WITH INSIGHTS AGENT
articles.summary: PlanetScale's database optimization agent added an index that made a production query slower because its SQL summary hid a 645-element IN list. Removing that list and filtering the small result set in Ruby cut average query time from 28.5 milliseconds to 1.95 milliseconds. Another change reordered a feature flag check, reducing database lookups from 28.7 million to 8.3 million per day.

articles.title: TOPTAL LAUNCHES TOPTAL AI: ONE PARTNER FOR ALL YOUR AI NEEDS
articles.summary: Toptal AI is a new full-stack AI services company that develops, evaluates, and deploys frontier-grade AI using open-weight and proprietary models, while organizations retain full ownership and control over their AI systems and data. Toptal AI acts as the single partner for all of their AI ambitions.

articles.title: AN AI OBSERVABILITY FRAMEWORK FOR YOUR AGENTIC APPLICATIONS
articles.summary: AWS authors propose an observability framework for agentic applications that crosses four layers with three concerns: reliability, cost, and security. They recommend OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions and evaluation gates, arguing that agents rarely fail with errors and often return confident wrong answers.

articles.title: THE LAYER OF YOUR PLATFORM NOBODY OWNS
articles.summary: Platform teams standardize nearly everything except the operating system under their clusters. Developers should use an immutable, API-managed OS such as Talos Linux, with declarative configuration and atomic upgrades, at the cost of losing interactive shell access.

articles.title: 87% OF THE ANTHROPIC POWER WILL COME FROM GAS AND 11% FROM COAL IN 2028
articles.summary: A case study estimates that Anthropic could emit 32 million metric tons of carbon dioxide in 2028. About 87% of its US power will come from gas and 11% from coal that year, with no direct renewable energy commitments in the US as of November.

articles.title: INCIDENTS IN THE NEWS
articles.summary: Surfing Complexity rounds up nine IT incidents reported between November 12 and 17, including an FAA ground stop, a Workday disaster recovery site writing to production databases, and a United outage. None involved cyberattacks.
